From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Benchmark plan follow-up (latency/throughput)

Chris/Marissa \u0014 quick technical notes for reproducibility (putting commands here so they're easy to copy):

- Recommended baseline: model=redwood-7b-q4, batch_size=8, concurrent_clients=80, max_tokens=1024
- To measure cold-start: start with empty runtime, run a single warmup request, then restart runtime and measure first N requests (we log first_request_ms)
- For tail-latency: set sampling window to 1s buckets and capture p99 over 10-minute steady-state window
- Disable continuous batching to mirror Bedrock's single-request-per-connection behavior if you want lower jitter (continuous_batching=false)

Example run (docker):
$ docker run --rm -e MODEL=redwood-7b-q4 redwood/bench:v1 /run_bench.sh --batch_size 8 --concurrency 80 --duration 600 --out results.csv

I'll attach the run-configs we used internally (small text file) \u0014 they include environment flags, CPU pinning, and kernel hints that can change p95 by ~10-15ms in tight tests.

Two suggested A/B variants to include:
A) Low-latency: batch_size=1, concurrency=40
B) High-throughput: batch_size=16, concurrency=160

If you'd like, we can provision a temporary Dedicated pool for an apples-to-apples run (isolated hardware) \u0014 Neha can follow up on credits/short-term capacity.

- Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: run-configs-logan-20260327.txt]
